core_obligations: Choose the \'etale charts: V \to Y surjective \'etale, U \to X \times_Y V surjective \'etale, and U_i \to X_i \times_X U surjective \'etale for each i (proof lines 2596-2603).

Verify that {X_i \times_X U \to U} is a \tau-covering, that each {U_i \to X_i \times_X U} is an \'etale hence \tau-covering, so that {U_i \to U} is a \tau-covering of schemes over S (proof lines 2605-2612).

Read off the displayed chain f has P_spaces <=> U \to V has P <=> each U_i \to V has P <=> each X_i \to Y has P_spaces, where the outer equivalences are the definition of P_spaces and the middle one is \tau-locality on the source of P (proof lines 2614-2621).
proof_roadmap: Reduce everything to schemes via surjective \'etale charts.
Check the covering conditions propagate through base change and \'etale refinement.
Unfold the definition of P_spaces along the chart and apply \tau-locality of P.
difficulty_reason: The proof is a covering-refinement chain: pick \'etale charts V \to Y, U \to X \times_Y V, U_i \to X_i \times_X U, note the composites give \tau-coverings by schemes, and read off the displayed three-step equivalence f has P_spaces <=> U \to V has P <=> each U_i \to V has P <=> each X_i \to Y has P_spaces, whose middle step is exactly \tau-locality on the source for the scheme property. The chart selection and the bookkeeping that \{U_i \to U\} is a \tau-covering of schemes are the substance.
